rationale: MVNT is a tumor of the cerebral hemispheres (temporal, parietal, frontal, occipital lobes; rare deep supratentorial sites); it is not reported in the spinal cord or cauda equina, a proper subset of the code ceiling which also includes C720/C721.
source_name: Calandrelli et al., Diagnostics 2025 (PMC11817111)

rationale: A generic (NOS) glioneuronal descriptor without a specific anatomic restriction; occurs across the CNS sites of the ceiling.
source_name: Yarabarla et al., Front Oncol 2023 — WHO 2021 intracranial meningiomas update (PMC10477988)

rationale: Myxoid glioneuronal tumor has a predilection for the septum pellucidum, corpus callosum and periventricular white matter of the lateral ventricle — all supratentorial cerebral structures; not reported in the spinal cord or cauda equina, a proper subset of the ceiling.
source_name: Lucas et al., myxoid glioneuronal tumor PDGFRA (PMID 31609499)

rationale: Papillary glioneuronal tumor is supratentorial in ~97% of cases (cerebral hemispheres, periventricular white matter), with only rare brainstem cases and no spinal cord involvement reported; a proper subset of the ceiling excluding C720/C721.
source_name: Du et al., imaging of PGNT (PMC11035433)

rationale: Although classically a fourth-ventricle/cerebellar tumor, RGNT is reported across the neuraxis including brainstem, pineal region, optic chiasm, ventricles and spinal cord; it spans essentially the full ceiling.
source_name: Clinical Case Reports 2021 — RGNT of fourth ventricle (PMC8369514)

rationale: DLGNT is defined by diffuse leptomeningeal spread over both the brain surface and the spinal cord, with common intraparenchymal spinal lesions; it involves the whole neuraxis, not a proper subset of the ceiling.
